bullets.text: Q3 CR 92.5; YTD CR 92.9; target CR 96; net income +27% Q3 (+5% YTD); special lines exceeded expectations across seasonal patterns; Commercial Lines rebounded profitably following 2012–2013 rate increases.

Quarterly growth matched year-to-date results at 6%. Direct auto recorded recent double-digit monthly written premium increases; Commercial Lines reported premium growth; special lines produced more muted growth.

Direct auto grew nicely with recent double-digit monthly written premium increases. Agency auto growth was disappointing; new applications fell off notably, retention lagged Direct auto, and management is responding with product modifications.

Personal Lines Direct new applications and PIF grew in the 7% range, increasingly with multi-product customers; Agency new applications fell off notably; Commercial Lines unit growth expected to mirror premium growth.

Service Centers reached 65 with three co-located openings, handling about 25% of repairable vehicles nationwide. Claims operations operate at their lowest loss adjustment expense level and highest claim quality.

Early auto frequency trends mitigated, and current rate levels have been largely sustainable longer. Recent personal injury protection severity recognition has company attention; auto margins operate better than, but close to, target expectations.

Net income was sluggish, up 27% in Q3 and 5% YTD, alongside frustratingly lower contributions from risk-matched investment choices. Frustration will not cause deviation from the company's strong, sustainable business plan.

Agency Snapshot acceptance in Massachusetts was notably higher with tested design changes; rollout to other states is expected late this year through 2015. The two-state renters product started gaining market acceptance.

Third-quarter results needed less qualification for weather events. The Hurricane Center's assessment of higher chances for a below-average season is playing out to-date; Progressive remains prepared and adequately priced, noting it only takes one.

Progress continued toward the 'Destination Era' strategic positioning. Co-located Service Centers serve as an important factor in expanding customer focus; overall, progress across almost every front builds from a solid market position.
